# skia / parse_path

skia's own fuzz target `parse_path` ([source](source/FuzzParsePath.cpp), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over skia (skia.googlesource.com/skia at 24a8072e).

Checks one property, an invariant: SkParsePath::FromSVGString, then ToSVGString in Absolute and Relative encodings; abort if either output starts with "Impossible". The comment says the test exists only to keep the output from being optimised away; it does not reparse or compare, so it is effectively trivially true.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against skia at commit 24a8072e with 1 patch to the library (listed on the project page).
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source differs from the upstream file at the pinned commit; the copy in source/ is the file as built.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing, so a statement about it says only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer.
